lead.question: 人终将老去，如何才能不惧死亡、安然度过晚年？哲学家罗素给出的答案是什么？
lead.warmup: 伯特兰·罗素是英国哲学家、数学家。这篇随笔写于他年近八旬之时，语调平和而豁达。作者从老年人对死亡的恐惧谈起，提出把个人兴趣逐渐向外扩展、忘掉小我，像河流汇入大海一样融入更广阔的生命。文章比喻生动，说理从容，是英语散文中的名篇。读时注意它层层递进的逻辑与凝练的用词。
goals: 理解“逐渐扩大兴趣、超越小我”这一核心观点及其河流比喻
掌握 oppressed by、impersonal、abject and ignoble、the decay of vitality 等表达
学会用定语从句和 since 引导的原因从句组织复合句
体会英语议论散文说理从容、比喻贴切的文体特点
lead.summary: 有些老年人因怕死而烦恼，但饱经甘苦、功成事毕的老人若仍怕死，就显得可怜可鄙。罗素认为，最好的办法是让兴趣日益广泛忘我，使自我之墙渐渐退去，生命融入宇宙的生命。个人存在如河流，由窄而宽，最终无声汇入大海。这样看待一生的人不会惧死；他愿工作到死，因为事业有人接续。
lead.tips: 易错：the best way to overcome it 中 to overcome 是不定式作定语，别写成 overcoming；主语 The best way 是单数，谓语用 is 而非 are。

questions.q: What, according to the author, is the best way to overcome the fear of death as you get older?
questions.zh: 按照作者的说法，人上了年纪后，克服对死亡的恐惧的最好办法是什么？
questions.a: To make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal, until bit by bit the walls of the ego recede and your life becomes increasingly merged in the universal life.
questions.aZh: 逐渐使自己的兴趣更加广泛、更加忘我，直到自我的围墙一点点退去，生命渐渐融入整个宇宙的生命。
questions.hint: 见课文第五句 The best way to overcome it ... is to make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal...

questions.q: Why does the author say the fear of death is justifiable in the young?
questions.zh: 作者为什么说青年人对死亡的恐惧是情有可原的？
questions.a: Because young men who have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle may justifiably feel bitter in the thought that they have been cheated of the best things life has to offer.
questions.aZh: 因为有理由担心自己会战死沙场的年轻人，一想到自己被剥夺了生活所能给予的最美好的东西，感到痛苦是理所应当的。
questions.hint: 见课文第二、三句 the young / killed in battle / cheated of the best things...

questions.q: What simile does the author use to describe an individual human existence, and how does it change?
questions.zh: 作者用什么比喻来形容个人的存在？这一比喻又如何变化？
questions.a: He compares it to a river: small at first and narrowly contained within its banks, rushing passionately past boulders and over waterfalls, then growing wider and flowing more quietly, until at last it merges painlessly in the sea.
questions.aZh: 他把个人存在比作河流：起初很小、被紧紧夹在两岸之间，热情奔放地冲过巨石、飞下瀑布，然后河面渐宽、水流渐缓，最后毫无痛苦地汇入大海。
questions.hint: 见课文第六、七句 like a river / grows wider / merged in the sea...

questions.q: How does the author wish to die, and why is the thought of rest not unwelcome?
questions.zh: 作者希望怎样死去？他为什么说长眠之念“未尝不是一件好事情”？
questions.a: He would wish to die while still at work, knowing that others will carry on what he can no longer do and content that what was possible has been done; as vitality decays and weariness increases, the thought of rest is not unwelcome.
questions.aZh: 他希望工作到死为止，因为知道有人会继续他未竟的事业，想到能做的都做了也就坦然；随着精力衰退、倦意增长，长眠之念也就不再令人反感。
questions.hint: 见课文第八、九句 the decay of vitality / I should wish to die while still at work...

questions.q: The author calls the fear of death in a fulfilled old man 'abject and ignoble'. Do you agree that widening one's impersonal interests can overcome it? Give your reasons.
questions.zh: 作者认为，饱经沧桑、功成事毕的老人若仍怕死就“可怜又可鄙”。你同意“让兴趣日益广泛忘我”能克服这种恐惧吗？请说明理由。
questions.a: Open-ended. A possible answer: Yes. When one's interests reach beyond the self, one's life merges with what will continue after death — in science, art, or the welfare of others — so personal extinction loses its terror; one dies content that the work goes on.
questions.aZh: 开放性作答。参考：同意。当兴趣超越小我，生命便融入死后仍将延续的事业（科学、艺术或他人的福祉），个人的消亡不再可怕，人也就能坦然工作到死。
questions.hint: 结合课文第五、八、九句作答，言之成理即可。

exercises.q: 汉译英：有些老年人因怕死而感到烦恼。
exercises.a: Some old people are oppressed by the fear of death.

exercises.q: 汉译英：老年人的怕死有点可怜又可鄙。
exercises.a: The fear of death in an old man is somewhat abject and ignoble.

exercises.q: 用括号中词的适当形式填空：The best way ___ (overcome) it is to make your interests more ___ (impersonal).
exercises.note: 不定式作定语，impersonal 作表语

exercises.q: 句型转换：将两句合并为含定语从句的复合句。Young men may feel bitter. / They have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle.
exercises.a: Young men who have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle may feel bitter.

exercises.q: 改错：The best way to overcome it are to make your interests wider.
exercises.note: 主语 the best way 为单数

exercises.q: 句型转换：用 since 把后句改写为原因状语从句。He will not suffer from the fear of death. / The things he cares for will continue.
exercises.a: He will not suffer from the fear of death, since the things he cares for will continue.
exercises.note: since 引导原因状语从句

exercises.q: 改错：Others will carry on that I can no longer do.

quiz.q: 作者认为克服对死亡恐惧的最好办法是什么？
options: To make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal.
To live a quiet life alone by a river.
To think about death as little as possible.
To leave all your work to others.

quiz.q: 作者为什么认为年轻人的怕死情有可原？
options: Because young men are naturally afraid of pain.
Because young men have known few joys and sorrows.
Because young men may be killed in battle and be cheated of life's best things.
Because young men have done nothing worthwhile.
quiz.note: 见第三句 killed in battle

quiz.q: 作者把个人的存在比作什么？
options: A waterfall.
A river.
A boulder.
The sea.
quiz.note: like a river 是中心比喻

quiz.q: 作者用 abject and ignoble 形容什么？
options: The death of a soldier in battle.
The weariness of old age.
The interests of young people.
The fear of death in an old man who has known joys and sorrows.
quiz.note: 见第四句 in an old man

quiz.q: 作者希望自己怎样死去？
options: While still at work, knowing that others will carry on what he can no longer do.
Peacefully in his sleep at home.
Far away from his family and friends.
Long before his vitality decays.
quiz.note: 见末句 die while still at work

quiz.q: the walls of the ego recede 意思最接近？
options: The walls of the house fall down.
One becomes more self-centred.
One loses all interest in life.
The sense of self gradually gives way.
quiz.note: ego 指自我，recede 指退去
